newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON SAYS ALL TOP ATHLETES TAKE DRUGS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON SAYS ALL TOP ATHLETES TAKE DRUGS.

text.p: Suspended Canadian sprinter Ben Johnson has accused world athletics bodies of making him a scapegoat and said that all top athletes took drugs.

"I am a victim of sport. All the elite athletes I know take drugs, even those who are held up as examples. I don't know anyone who is completely clean," Johnson said in an interview published Wednesday in the La Nacion daily in Buenos Aires, where he is working as a personal trainer on the latest comeback by soccer star Diego Maradona.
"Everyone runs fast, but they grab hold of some of them and they pay the price for the rest," he said.

Johnson, who is awaiting an International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) ruling this month on his appeal against a life-ban for exceeding testosterone limits, said that Canadian and world athletics bodies were to blame for his plight.

"The Canadian federation always knew that all the athletes on the team used drugs to improve their performance. It's a business. They give you a hand because they're making money and with the other hand they shoot you," he said.

"This all has to do with money and power. The president of the International Amateur Athletic Federation, the Italian Primo Nebiolo, offers $50,000 for breaking world records and on the other hand he asks for people to play clean. What's an athlete going to think?" Johnson said.
The 35-year-old was confident he could still win if he were allowed back on the tracks.

"I know I am the fastest athlete in the world, and no one argues with that," he said, "My only crime was to run very fast. Drugs aren't enough for a world record, but they can help you with 25 percent of a good time."

Nonetheless, Johnson agreed that drugs are a problem: "I think that everyone should follow a single rule: don't use drugs. Why doesn't the IAAF, if it wants to get to the bottom of the problem, grant an amnesty, and let each athlete confess without any penalty, so that we could start again with clean athletics?"

Johnson was stripped of his Olympic Gold medal at Seoul for testing positive for steroids after winning the 100 meters in a world record 9.791 seconds. He made a comeback three years later, but was banned for life after failing a dope test in Toronto in 1993.
Johnson's new charge Maradona, embarked on his fifth comeback, has also had problems with drug controls, and was kicked out of the World Cup finals in 1994 in the United States after failing a test.
